description: Rust backend plus thin frontend wrappers. Independent of FEAT-001/002 (only Rust + src/services/qrDeviceService.ts + src/types/qrDevice.ts). Review findings addressed here: carried-over HIGH shell-quoting fix for launch_deep_link (sh_quote + build_launch_args + Rust tests), rqrr exact pin with default-features=false, and NIT 4 (stable send-to-device filename hash: Cargo.toml already has sha2 0.11.0, so use the first 4 bytes of SHA-256; no FNV fallback needed). Adds exactly one Cargo dependency (rqrr) which MUST be reported to the user in the final handoff. launch_deep_link's argument shape to the frontend does not change.
steps: Read context.json, design.md 6.0-6.3 and 7.3, design-review.md finding 4; read src-tauri/src/deep_link.rs fully, src-tauri/src/screenshot.rs (capture_png_frame signature, validate_png, sanitize_filename_component ~l.222), src-tauri/src/adb.rs (validate_serial, validate_package_name, run_adb_text), src-tauri/src/lib.rs mod list and invoke_handler (~l.226), and one existing use of sha2 (grep -rn "Sha256" src-tauri/src) to copy the 0.11 API style. Run `rustc --version` and confirm >= 1.85.1 (local is 1.96.0); Cargo.toml has no rust-version key, do not add one.

src-tauri/src/deep_link.rs: add `pub(crate) fn sh_quote(s: &str) -> String { format!("'{}'", s.replace('\'', r"'\''")) }` and `fn build_launch_args(uri: &str, pkg: Option<&str>) -> Vec<String>` producing shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d <sh_quote(uri)> [-p <sh_quote(pkg)>]; make launch_deep_link use it (keep validate_uri, validate_serial, validate_package_name and the 'Activity not started' detection unchanged). Rust tests in the existing #[cfg(test)] mod: -d value exactly `'https://x/?a=1&b=2'`; `a;reboot` -> `'a;reboot'`; `$(id)` -> `'$(id)'`; a backtick URI quoted; `it's` -> `'it'\''s'`; URI with space quoted; -p value quoted; validate_uri still rejects empty and control characters. Then grep frontend tests that assert launch_deep_link invoke arguments (`grep -rn "launch_deep_link" src`) and confirm none depend on raw argv (the invoke argument shape is unchanged).

src-tauri/Cargo.toml: add exactly `rqrr = { version = "=0.11.0", default-features = false }`. After `cargo build`, run `cargo tree -e features -i rqrr` (no `img` feature may appear) and `cargo tree -d | grep -i '^image'` (single image version).

Create src-tauri/src/qr_device.rs and register `mod qr_device;` and the three commands in src-tauri/src/lib.rs next to deep_link::generate_qr_svg. Result structs are serde-serialisable with success/error_code/error like DeepLinkResult. (1) `qr_send_to_device(serial, filename, png_base64, custom_path) -> QrDeviceResult`: validate serial (adb::validate_serial), decode base64, reject > 8 MB or non-PNG (screenshot::validate_png), name = format!("{stem}-{hash8}.png") where stem = sanitize_filename_component(stem_of(filename)) truncated to 80 chars (char-safe) and hash8 = lowercase hex of the first 4 bytes of Sha256 over the PNG bytes via a pure `fn short_hash(bytes: &[u8]) -> String`; write bytes to a uniquely named temp file in the OS temp dir, run `adb -s <serial> push <tmp> /sdcard/Download/<name>` through adb::run_adb_text (array args), best-effort `shell am broadcast -a android.intent.action.MEDIA_SCANNER_SCAN_FILE -d <sh_quote("file:///sdcard/Download/<name>")>` (failure ignored, result field scan:false), always delete the temp file; result {success, path_on_device, scan, error_code, error}. Expose the pure `fn build_remote_name(filename:&str, bytes:&[u8]) -> String` for tests. (2) `qr_decode_image(bytes_base64) -> DecodeResult{success,texts,error_code,error}`: validate base64, decoded <= 10 MB, png/jpeg only (guess format; webp/gif -> unsupported_format), dimensions <= 8000x8000, run decode inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking via a pure `fn decode_qr_from_luma(width, height, &[u8]) -> Vec<String>` using `rqrr::PreparedImage::prepare_from_greyscale(w, h, |x, y| luma[y*w+x])`, `grids()` and `grid.decode()` per grid; error codes invalid_input, too_large, unsupported_format, no_qr_found. (3) `qr_capture_and_decode(serial, custom_path) -> {success, texts, thumbnail_png_base64, error_code, error}`: `const QR_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 30;` local to qr_device.rs passed to screenshot::capture_png_frame (do not touch the screenshot module's private const), decode the full frame with the same helper, downscale a thumbnail to <= 480 px wide with image::imageops::resize (Triangle) and re-encode as PNG; never write the frame to disk; empty texts is a valid success (UI says no QR found). Log failures with the project's existing eprintln!/logging approach.

Rust tests in qr_device.rs #[cfg(test)] (no ADB): build_remote_name always ends in .png even for `a.exe` and `../x`, stem capped at 80 chars on multibyte input, empty stem -> `device-<hash>.png`, same bytes -> same name, different bytes -> different name, and short_hash is a fixed known vector (assert the hex of a literal byte string so stability across builds is pinned); decode round trip: generate with the `qrcode` crate, render to a luma image buffer with a quiet zone and module scaling, encode PNG with `image`, then run the same validation+decode path and assert equal text; also JPEG round trip; invalid base64, oversize (> 10 MB), non-image bytes, unsupported format, blank image -> no_qr_found.

Frontend: src/types/qrDevice.ts (QrDeviceResult, QrDecodeResult, QrCaptureResult) and src/services/qrDeviceService.ts with decodeQrImage(bytesBase64), sendQrToDevice(serial, filename, pngBase64, customPath), captureAndDecode(serial, customPath) as thin invoke<T> wrappers in the style of src/services/deepLinkService.ts (command names qr_decode_image, qr_send_to_device, qr_capture_and_decode; camelCase argument keys as Tauri expects). Add src/services/qrDeviceService.test.ts mocking @tauri-apps/api/core invoke and asserting command names and argument keys.

Run all verification commands (use timeout >= 900000 ms for the first cargo build); commit `feat(qr): quote deep-link shell args, add QR device and decode commands` staging src-tauri/Cargo.toml (Cargo.lock is gitignored), src-tauri/src/*.rs and the frontend files.
acceptance_criteria: `cd src-tauri && cargo test --lib` passes including the new deep_link quoting tests and qr_device tests
`cd src-tauri && cargo build` succeeds with the new dependency
`cargo tree -e features -i rqrr` shows no img feature and `cargo tree -d | grep -i '^image'` shows one version
Cargo.toml contains exactly one added dependency line: rqrr = { version = "=0.11.0", default-features = false }
launch_deep_link quotes the -d and -p values and the invoke argument shape is unchanged (existing frontend deep-link tests still pass)
verification: cd src-tauri && cargo tree -e features -i rqrr
findings: DONE (committed locally on main, 'feat(qr): quote deep-link shell args, add QR device and decode commands'). NEW CARGO DEPENDENCY TO REPORT TO THE USER IN THE FINAL HANDOFF: rqrr = { version = "=0.11.0", default-features = false } (only added dependency; Cargo.lock is gitignored so the = pin in Cargo.toml is the only committed pin). cargo tree -e features -i rqrr shows no img feature; cargo tree -d shows no duplicate image crate. Verified: cargo test --lib 278 passed (new deep_link quoting tests + 11 qr_device tests), cargo build OK, npx vitest run src/services/qrDeviceService.test.ts passes (3 tests), npx tsc --noEmit clean. NOTE: `src/components/deep-link-launcher` has no *.test.* files, so that vitest path matches nothing; no frontend test asserts launch_deep_link argv (only src/services/deepLinkService.ts references it), invoke argument shape unchanged. SECURITY FIX to mention in handoff: launch_deep_link now single-quotes the -d and -p values via deep_link::sh_quote (pub(crate)); URIs containing & now work instead of being truncated, and ; $() backticks no longer run on the device. FOR LATER STEPS: (1) Rust result structs serialise camelCase like DeepLinkResult: qr_send_to_device -> {success, pathOnDevice?, scan, error?, errorCode?}; qr_decode_image(bytesBase64) -> {success, texts, error?, errorCode?} with errorCode in invalid_input|too_large|unsupported_format|no_qr_found|decode_failed (blank/no-QR image => success:false, errorCode no_qr_found); qr_capture_and_decode -> {success, texts, thumbnailPngBase64?, error?, errorCode?} where empty texts with success:true means no QR on screen. Frontend types in src/types/qrDevice.ts (QrDeviceResult, QrDecodeResult, QrCaptureResult); service fns decodeQrImage(bytesBase64), sendQrToDevice(serial, filename, pngBase64, customPath?), captureAndDecode(serial, customPath?) in src/services/qrDeviceService.ts. Other error codes from send: too_large (>8MB), invalid_input (bad base64 / not PNG), temp_file_failed, plus adb codes (device_offline, device_unauthorized, invalid_serial, failed ...). (2) Remote filename is '<sanitized stem<=80 chars>-<first 4 bytes of SHA-256 hex>.png' in /sdcard/Download; sanitize_filename_component keeps non-ASCII, so UI text should say 'Downloads/<name>' from pathOnDevice rather than predicting the name. (3) rqrr cannot read inverted (light-on-dark) codes; note generate_qr_svg's preview palette is light-on-dark, so decoding a screenshot of a dark-mode QR may return no_qr_found. Not handled (out of scope). (4) rqrr's grid API is detect_grids() (design text said grids()); rqrr decode() returns UTF-8 String only. (5) rustc 1.96.0, no rust-version added.
